If you want creative without paying for a big-agency structure, I’d compare a handful of Toronto independents/studios rather than traditional agencies. Here’s a useful shortlist:

Studio	Why compare them	Published pricing / positioning
Avenel	Specifically focused on independent Toronto businesses; has work for cafés, restaurants, salons and shops	Launch sites from $800, full sites from $1,200; about 2 weeks 
Avenel

Lorven	More art-directed/custom feel; small studio, custom-coded rather than templates	Doesn't publish a simple starting price; emphasizes bespoke design and direct founder/studio involvement 
Lorven
+1

Oluma	Two-person studio with strong visual design, motion and e-commerce capabilities	Premium independent-studio positioning; 5–8 week average delivery 
Oluma Agency

Ca Ching Designs	Particularly worth comparing if your shop sells products online	Shopify-focused, with web design/e-commerce consulting and an emphasis on design detail
Codee	Small-business websites plus e-commerce, branding and custom development	Toronto-based; custom sites without templates or platform lock-in 
Codee

Marrelay	Founder-led and broader technically—useful if the site needs unusual functionality	Fixed-price quotes, weekly demos, Shopify/Webflow development and e-commerce 
Marrelay
How I'd structure the comparison

For a Toronto retail shop, ask each for the same brief:

5–8 page website

Strong visual/brand direction

Mobile-first

Store location, hours and Google Maps

Product/menu/service showcase

Instagram integration

Basic local SEO

Contact/inquiry functionality

Optional Shopify/e-commerce

You own the domain, site and accounts

Fixed project price, not an open-ended hourly engagement

That makes the quotes much easier to compare. As a rough benchmark, one Toronto studio currently publishes $2,500 starting for a marketing site and $6,000 for commerce, while smaller studios advertise considerably lower entry points. 
Website Co.
+1

For your particular goal, I'd put Avenel, Lorven, Oluma, and Ca Ching Designs on the initial comparison list—they represent meaningfully different approaches rather than four versions of the same agency model.
